title: add benchmark-lab profiling baselines and reporting pipeline v75
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: our profiling baselines and reporting pipeline had diverged from the representative workload runners used in recent adaptive-batching experiments. This PR brings the profiling baselines and the reporting pipeline to parity with the latest runner changes (v75), improves reproducibility for cold-start and KV-cache scenarios, and adds incremental observability to the reporting output.

Summary of changes: added new representative workload runner configs for multi-variant scenarios, extended profiling baseline harness to capture cold-start and steady-state traces, introduced a reporting pipeline job (airflow + dagster wrapper) that produces per-run artifacts (latency histograms, memory profiles, kernel selection logs) and uploads standardized bundles to the benchmark S3 bucket. Also added a schema update for the reporting JSON and small docs for running locally.

What this PR includes: checklist: - [x] representative workload runner configs for v75 (conversational, long-context, embeddings-heavy) - [x] profiling harness extensions (cold-start sampler, steady-state samplers, KV-cache warmup) - [x] reporting pipeline DAG and helper scripts - [x] standardized reporting schema v2 -> added schema_v2.json - [x] unit and integration tests for new runner options - [x] docs and README updates for local reproduction

Testing and validation: ran benchmark CI with the new runners across p3/rtx and a40 nodes; perf regression checks (baseline vs v75) passed within allowed thresholds. Cold-start regression test added to benchmark-lab CI and executed successfully. Manual validation: sampled generated reporting bundles and verified schema, included histogram and flamegraph attachments.

Rollout plan: merge to main, deploy the reporting DAG in staging, run nightly profiling jobs for two weeks, monitor regression alerts in SLO-dashboard. If regressions detected, revert the DAG and revert the runner config tag.

Notes: no customer-facing API changes. This PR intentionally keeps runner defaults unchanged; new runners are opt-in via benchmark job config.
